title: B2B Split Payment with Customer Credit and ERP Credit Gate

context.summary: A wholesale distributor needs to support net-30 payment terms at checkout without replacing SmartCheckout. ERP credit limits must be enforced in real time before order placement to prevent over-credit exposure.
painPoints: No native net-terms / purchase-order payment support in SmartCheckout
ERP holds live credit limits that must be validated before order confirmation
Finance team requires same-day reconciliation between VTEX orders and ERP credit accounts
constraints: Must not require a fully custom checkout implementation
Must integrate with existing ERP credit management module
Solution must be PCI-compliant without introducing new card data paths

solution.pattern: Customer Credit + real-time ERP credit gate
solution.summary: Leverage VTEX Customer Credit as the payment method for net-terms orders. A lightweight VTEX IO middleware app intercepts the orderForm before placement, calls ERP credit management via REST, and either approves or holds the order. Approved orders flow normally; held orders trigger a notification workflow.

keyDecisions.decision: Use VTEX IO middleware for the ERP credit check instead of a standalone external service
keyDecisions.rationale: Keeps the integration inside the VTEX platform boundary, simplifies deployment and monitoring, and avoids an additional infrastructure component to maintain.
alternativesConsidered: External API gateway proxying the ERP call
ERP-side webhook pushing credit status to VTEX

keyDecisions.decision: Use order hold state (status: payment-pending) as the async fallback when ERP response exceeds 3 seconds
keyDecisions.rationale: Prevents checkout timeout failures from becoming lost orders. Finance reviews held orders within 1 business hour — acceptable SLA for B2B.
alternativesConsidered: Reject order immediately on ERP timeout (too disruptive for B2B buyers)
Allow order and reconcile post-placement (unacceptable credit risk)

solution.implementationNotes: ERP credit management API must support OAuth 2.0 client credentials — verify authentication requirements with the ERP operations team early. VTEX Customer Credit requires a manual credit limit setup per buyer account before go-live; plan for a data migration sprint if an existing credit book already lives in the ERP.

pros: No custom checkout — SmartCheckout UX is preserved, reducing implementation risk
VTEX Customer Credit is a native product — no additional licencing cost
Real-time credit enforcement prevents over-exposure before order confirmation
IO middleware pattern is reusable across similar B2B scenarios with the same ERP integration
cons: ERP latency at checkout introduces a blocking call — p99 latency must be < 2s or UX degrades
Customer Credit UI has limited customisation — complex approval workflows (multi-level PO approval) are not supported natively
Credit limits must be maintained in both VTEX Customer Credit and ERP — dual-master risk if sync is not automated

risks.risk: ERP API latency at checkout exceeds acceptable threshold
risks.mitigation: Implement async fallback with order hold state and a 3-second timeout. Monitor p95/p99 at ERP API gateway and alert if > 1.5s.

risks.risk: Credit limit dual-master divergence between VTEX and ERP
risks.mitigation: Implement a nightly ERP → VTEX Customer Credit sync job. Alert finance team on sync failure.

risks.risk: VTEX Customer Credit does not support partial credit approval
risks.mitigation: Document this limitation during solution discovery. If partial approval is required, escalate to headless checkout pattern.

recommendedWhen: Buyer organization already uses or is open to VTEX Customer Credit
Net-30 / net-60 terms are the primary non-standard payment requirement
ERP credit management has a stable REST API with < 1s p95 latency
Multi-level PO approval workflows are NOT required
avoidWhen: Complex multi-level purchase order approval workflows are required
ERP is not capable of real-time synchronous API responses (batch-only)
Use case requires partial credit approval at line-item level
Credit book exceeds 50,000 accounts and real-time sync is not feasible

classification.architecturePattern: Event-driven middleware with native payment extension
